<reason>Both sides were sharp, but CON built the cleaner decisive line: the motion's marginal reach is exactly the non-threatening posters ("interesting that she works there"), and separating a raid from a viral movement at that layer requires judging raid-vs-movement and private-vs-public — a check that "immediate" removes. PRO's Rebuttal 2 effectively conceded this by softening "immediate" to "hours, against the cluster the evidence identifies" and adding a "private-figure target" rider, which CON correctly named as review. PRO's strongest attack (the organizer who never posts removable content; fragmented doxxing) was answered directly and plausibly by CON's A1/A2 — vulnerability disclosures and locating details are already actionable content — leaving only a small residual PRO could call a blind spot. PRO also damaged its own credibility by declaring in Rebuttal 2 that "no answer came" to its pressure questions when CON's answering turn had not yet occurred, then built its "decision point" on that phantom silence. PRO's closing gotcha (CON also relied on "private person") was clever and rhetorically the best single move, but CON's closing had the last word and reasonably distinguished a sentence that carries its own harm from a sentence that carries none. PRO's reversibility asymmetry stayed live but was contested rather than unanswered. Clear but competitive CON win.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's A4.5–A4.6: after PRO listed its observable campaign signals, CON showed they match every viral callout, then pointed out PRO had to add an unobservable "private-figure" rider and redefine "immediate" as hours of evidence-identification — "PRO has conceded the check I demanded and kept the word that denies it." PRO's closing counter that CON also judged context was the sharpest reply, but only partially blunted it.</best_rebuttal>
